headline: UN envoy urges Australia to act on 'embarrassing' Indigenous rights record
description: Albert Barume is expected to present his full findings to the UN Human Rights Council in September next year
author: Reuters
article_text:
Australia must take urgent action to protect Indigenous peoples’ rights, a United Nations expert warned, describing the country’s record as “embarrassing” and damaging to its international reputation, according to local broadcaster ABC on Friday.

Albert Barume, the UN special rapporteur on the rights of Indigenous peoples, made the remarks after a two-week visit to Australia, during which he was denied access to youth detention centers in Queensland and the Northern Territory.

"I'm convinced Indigenous peoples' rights … are unsafe in the hands of states and territories," Barume told reporters in Sydney. "The state of protection of Indigenous peoples' rights is a bit embarrassing."

Barume urged the government to introduce legally binding national minimum standards aligned with the UN Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples, warning that protections currently depend too heavily on state and territory governments.

He said changes in government could reverse existing progress, leaving Indigenous rights vulnerable to political priorities.

The envoy also raised concerns over punitive bail and sentencing laws, which he said had contributed to the disproportionate imprisonment of Indigenous children.

First Nations children account for nearly two-thirds of those in youth detention, while Indigenous Australians make up 37% of the country's prison population, compared with 24% in 2009.

His preliminary findings also highlighted concerns over racism, violence against Indigenous women, missing and murdered Indigenous people, and the high number of Indigenous children in out-of-home care.

Barume criticised the abandonment of treaty processes in Queensland and the Northern Territory, stressing that fundamental rights should not depend on election outcomes.

Despite the concerns, he acknowledged progress in areas including Indigenous-led organisations, ranger programmes, language revitalisation and native title rights.

He called on Prime Minister Anthony Albanese to take responsibility for addressing the situation, saying protecting Indigenous rights was in Australia's collective interest.

Barume is expected to present his full findings to the UN Human Rights Council in September next year.

headline: Tyga and Madelaine Petsch split after more than a year of dating
description: Their reported separation comes 2 months after the pair were seen enjoying a date at Knott’s Scary Farm in California
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Their reported separation comes 2 months after the pair were seen enjoying a date at Knott’s Scary Farm in California

Tyga and Madelaine Petsch have reportedly ended their relationship after more than a year of dating, with multiple sources confirming the split to PEOPLE.

The 36-year-old rapper and 32-year-old Riverdale actress first sparked romance rumours in February 2025, when they were spotted sitting courtside at a Los Angeles Lakers basketball game. Neither star publicly confirmed their relationship.

Their reported separation comes two months after the pair were seen enjoying an affectionate date at Knott’s Scary Farm in California.

At the time, a source told PEOPLE in September that “they’re really happy and she’s been spending time with his son too.”

The comment referred to Tyga’s 13-year-old son, King Cairo, whom he shares with his former partner Blac Chyna.

Throughout their rumoured relationship, Tyga and Petsch were spotted together at several public events, including the Vanity Fair and Instagram Vanities Party in February 2025.

They were also photographed leaving the event together and attending a gathering at Bar Marmont.

Petsch previously discussed her approach to relationships and privacy during an appearance on the Call Her Daddy podcast with Alex Cooper.

“I am at a place in my life where I’ve been a public figure for 10 years and I’ve tried to navigate my private and my public lives for a very long time, not very well,” she said.

The actress also highlighted the qualities she values in a partner, including “consistency”, kindness, communication and trust.

headline: Pakistan to host FIH Nations Cup
description: Ten nations are likely to feature in the tournament
author: Zulfiqar Baig
article_text:
Pakistan will host the next FIH Nations Cup, with ten international teams expected to compete in the tournament as the country steps up efforts to revive its fortunes in hockey.

International Hockey Federation’s (FIH) President Tayyab Ikram made the announcement at an event in Islamabad focused on the revival of Pakistan hockey.

The federal government also pledged its full support to the national federation.

Ikram said the Nations Cup was a major international competition, ranking among hockey's biggest events after the World Cup and the Olympic Games.

He also announced that the Naseer Bunda Hockey Stadium in Islamabad had been approved as an official FIH High Performance Centre, a move expected to support player development and improve training facilities.

The FIH president stressed that Pakistan needed to improve its hockey governance structure and invest in the national team's preparations if it hoped to return to the top level of international competition.

He said players needed financial support, modern training facilities and access to coaches who met international standards. Ikram also said India should come to Pakistan to play hockey.

Federal Minister for Inter-Provincial Coordination (IPC) Rana Sanaullah said hockey remained a source of national identity and pride, recalling Pakistan's history as a leading force in the sport.

However, he acknowledged that the country's recent performances had been disappointing and said Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif had directed the government to give hockey special attention.

"The government stands with the hockey federation," Sanaullah said, urging the PHF to prepare a comprehensive plan for the sport's revival.

He pledged that the government would provide players with the necessary facilities and support, while calling on senior former players to contribute to rebuilding the game.

Sanaullah also said Pakistan needed people committed to representing the country rather than those who had brought politics into hockey.

PHF president Mohyuddin Wani said efforts were being made at the government level to promote the sport and described the event as an important step towards a new era for Pakistan hockey.

National Assembly member Zeb Jaffar said hosting a ten-team international tournament would help promote hockey in the country. She described the agreement between the PHF and FIH as a milestone.

He pledged that the government would provide players with the necessary facilities and support, while calling on senior former players to contribute to rebuilding the game.
Sanaullah also said Pakistan needed people committed to representing the country rather than those who had brought politics into hockey.
PHF president Mohyuddin Wani said efforts were being made at the government level to promote the sport and described the event as an important step towards a new era for Pakistan hockey.
National Assembly member Zeb Jaffar said hosting a ten-team international tournament would help promote hockey in the country. She described the agreement between the PHF and FIH as a milestone.
